memory_candidates.content: git check-ignore reports an already-TRACKED path as NOT ignored, even when a .gitignore pattern matches it byte-for-byte -- gitignore rules never apply retroactively to tracked files, and check-ignore faithfully reflects that. Consequence for any lint/test that probes 'is this path ignored': if the probe path happens to coincide with a path that got force-tracked (git add -f) in a fixture or in real history, Check A-style ignore-coverage assertions will report a false 'not ignored' finding for that specific path even though the pattern itself is correct -- this is expected, not a bug in the pattern, and a regression test reproducing a tracked-file incident should expect BOTH the ignore-coverage check AND the tracked-file check to fail together on that path, then both to pass together once untracked.

When a markdown policy doc's fenced code block must stay byte-identical to a bash lib's generated output (because the doc can't `source` the lib), pin them with a dedicated regression-test case that extracts the fenced block via awk and diffs it against the lib function's stdout -- rather than trusting hand-maintenance. Demonstrate the pin is load-bearing with a deliberate-break check: temporarily desync one side, confirm the test goes red, restore. This is the doc-sync pattern that closes the 'N enumerations drift independently' defect class when one of the N sites is prose, not code.
